originalTitle: S&P 500, Nasdaq End Lower But Dow Rebounds As Traders Rotate Out Of AI — NVDA, SPCX, PANW In Focus
summary: The Nasdaq 100 briefly touched bear market territory on Wednesday before paring some losses.
content: The S&P 500 fell about 0.3%, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 0.6%, and the Dow Jones index rose 0.3% on Wednesday.Fed’s Beige Book showed rising price pressures, but at a moderate pace.The PCE index climbed 3.8% in October compared with a year earlier. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq ended lower on Wednesday, and fresh PCE and the Federal Reserve’s beige book hinted toward persistent price pressures, while the Dow Jones gained for the third straight session amid a shift out of AI.The S&P 500 fell about 0.3%, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 0.6%, and the Dow Jones index rose 0.3% on Wednesday. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, ended 0.7% higher. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) fell about 0.3%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) gained 0.3%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) dropped 0.7% on Wednesday. Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF fell between 0.5% and 1%, with Nvidia (NVDA), Micron Tech (MU) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) leading declines.Helping the Dow were gains in industrials, materials and financials stocks that gained between 0.8% and 2% as more investors rotate out of the AI play.Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was in ‘neutral’ territory around the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), ‘extremely bullish’ on the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) and ‘bearish’ on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA).US Market DriversIndexMoveCloseDow Jones Industrial Average0.3%50,182.95 S&P 500-0.3%7,182.78 Nasdaq 100-0.6%26,046.90 Eight out of 12 Federal Reserve’s regional banks reported rising price pressures and warned about the risk of an overheating economy, driven in part by heavy capital spending on artificial intelligence infrastructure. Commerce Department figures released Wednesday reinforced those concerns, showing gross domestic product expanded at a 4.3% annualized rate in the third quarter—its fastest pace in three years—propelled by the strongest surge in business investment since 2020.The regional feedback arrives alongside separate government data showing inflation remains stubbornly above the Fed's 2% target. The personal consumption expenditures price index, the central bank's preferred inflation gauge, climbed 3.8% in October compared with a year earlier. Core inflation, which strips out volatile food and energy costs, recorded its sharpest increase since 2023.Meanwhile, the Nasdaq 100 briefly touched bear market territory on Wednesday as more investors moved out of AI into other sectors like industrials, materials and financial services. Investors have pulled back sharply from tech shares in recent weeks as doubts grow over the financial return on massive AI infrastructure spending. A tepid reception which sent the share prices of Anthropic below its listing price coupled with unease around multiple federal and congressional hearings pertaining to Nvidia’s chip export practices have dampened sentiment.“There is still no end in sight for the heightened volatility as investors continue to unwind leveraged risky positions, and move into bonds and other haven assets,” Fawad Razaqzada at Stonex Trading and Forex.com told Bloomberg. Key Trending StocksShares of Palo Alto Networks (PANW) fell sharply in after-hours trading on Wednesday after reports that a former regional vice president has sued the cybersecurity company, alleging he was fired for raising concerns about accounting practices intended to inflate revenue. Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) share price ended lower for the second consecutive session on Wednesday after credit rating agency S&P Global Ratings announced it may lower its rating on the chipmaker by one notch following a 90-day review. Bankers at Morgan Stanley and Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc. are working to bring a $4.5 billion loan backed by graphics processing units to market as soon as next week for CoreWeave Inc., Bloomberg reported. Elon Musk’s ambitions to build orbital AI data centers received a major boost on Wednesday, after the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) authorized SpaceX (SPCX) to deploy up to one million satellites for its computing network. For updates and corrections, email newsroom[at]stocktwits[dot]com.
